title: Record $173.7B Sent Home, and a New US Tax on Cash Transfers | Across the Water, Ep. 6
lede: Migrants sent a record $173.7 billion home to Latin America and the Caribbean in 2025, the IDB estimates. Since Jan 1, 2026, a 1% US excise tax applies to transfers funded with cash, money orders or cashier's checks. This episode follows the money to the Dominican Republic, Jamaica and Haiti, explains how the tax works, and looks at why sending has kept rising.
keyPoints: Remittances to Latin America and the Caribbean hit a record $173.7 billion in 2025, up 7.3%; the Caribbean grew 10.8% (IDB).
The Dominican Republic received $9.49 billion in January–September 2026, up 6.5%; 80.9% of September's inflows came from the US (Banco Central de la República Dominicana).
Remittances were 15.4% of Jamaica's GDP in 2025; first-half 2026 inflows rose 4.2% to $1.78 billion (Bank of Jamaica).
Haiti received a record $4.4 billion in formal remittances in fiscal 2025, about 79% from the US (World Bank).
The 1% US tax (26 U.S.C. §4475, from Jan 1, 2026) covers cash-funded transfers; bank-account and US-card transfers are exempt. The IDB reports no significant impact so far.
